# technitium_api_token (Resource)

Issues an API token for a user, for tools that call the HTTP API. The token is only known when it is created, so an imported token has no `token` value. Changing the user or name issues a new token; destroying the resource revokes it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_api_token" "external_dns" {
  username   = technitium_user.external_dns.username
  token_name = "external-dns"
}

output "external_dns_token" {
  value     = technitium_api_token.external_dns.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `token_name` (String) A name for the token. Names need not be unique.
- `username` (String) The user the token acts as, in lower case.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.
- `partial_token` (String) The first 16 characters of the token, which the server shows to identify it. It is the import ID.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token, for the `Authorization: Bearer` header or the provider's `token`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The partial token, as shown under Administration → Sessions
terraform import technitium_api_token.external_dns 0123456789abcdef
```
